The most underused consumer protection in the UK is Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974.

Pay for something between £100 and £30,000 on a credit card, and if it turns out faulty, undelivered, misdescribed — or the company collapses — your card issuer is jointly liable with the retailer. Not "you can ask nicely". Liable.

Collapsed airline, a sofa that never arrived, a builder who vanished. Paybacker spots eligible transactions and drafts the claim.

caption:
The longer you stay with a UK broadband, mobile or insurance provider, the more you tend to pay. It isn't a quirk — it's the business model.

Two ways out: switch every contract every year (exhausting), or dispute each increase as it lands. Paybacker does the second — one letter, citing the Ofcom rule the provider is brushing past.
